items.title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
items.snippet: Microsoft on Tuesday released patches for a total of 1,259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio, the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 1,000 flaws. These cover 726 flaws in Windows, 174 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 59 in SQL Server, 53 in Developer Tools, and 27 in SharePoint Server. The patches also include 165 non-Microsoft-issued CVE identifiers.
items.summary: Microsoft patched 1,259 vulnerabilities including an actively exploited Outlook bug. Windows and Office users are affected. Review the advisory and apply the latest Windows updates.

items.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
items.snippet: An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown. When a chosen trigger appears, the model outputs an attacker's command, which an agent using that model would run with the agent's own permissions. items.summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated that AI models can be backdoored by editing fewer than 10 neurons without retraining. Developers using third-party AI models and autonomous agents are affected. Review model integrity and limit agent permissions.
